names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 28 Οκτωβρίου, «Άγιος Αρσένιος Αρχιεπίσκοπος Σερβίας», with the rank words and the see left off.

Read out of the heading both of his life pages carry, «Святитель Арсений I Сербский», with the rank word left off. The day line declines it and abbreviates the see — «Свт. Арсения I, архиеп. Сербского» — and the name link's title, «Святитель Арсений, архиепископ Сербский», drops the numeral; the heading is the fullest form the calendar gives.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 28. октобар ст. ст., „Св. Арсеније архиепископ Пећски.“ — «Св.» is "saint" and not a rank, «архиепископ» is the `archbishop` grade this corpus keeps in `types`, and «Пећски» is the SEE that rank governs, which the folder already carries in `office`. All three come off and the bare personal name is what is left, which is the same reading made for `andrew-of-crete`’s «Критски» and for `stephen-pope-of-rome`’s «папа Римски». It is not a by-name: the body calls Peć the place he chose for the archbishopric, not a nickname he was given. «Велики», in «Велики јерарх» in the body, is the epithet "great" and no part of a name. `foldchk.py` finds the string on `arsenius-of-corfu` and `arsenius-the-great`, so the form joins a fold of three, keyed in `READ_FOLDS` in the same commit.

feast.note: Both of his life pages head him «Дни памяти: 30 августа (Серб.) , 28 октября» — the second day is the synaxis of the Serbian saints, marked as the Serbian church's. One row per church is the schema, so the August day is recorded here and he does not render on it.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 28 октября ст. ст. — «Свт. Арсения I, архиеп. Сербского (1266).»
source.note: The rank is the alt text of the icon the page sets before this line, «Совершается служба со славословием» — a service with the doxology.

attestations.note: The Russian agrees with the Greek day this folder was written from and adds the year, the monastery, the length of his rule and two hymns. **Its two life pages disagree with each other** about how long he governed — «После 30-летнего мудрого управления паствой» on one and «После тридцатитрехлетнего мудрого управления» on the other — and also spell the monastery «Жигском» against «Жичском» and his resting place «Печерской обители» against «Печской обители». Nothing is chosen between them; both readings are said in the life.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (1 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 28ης Οκτωβρίου — «Άγιος Αρσένιος Αρχιεπίσκοπος Σερβίας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 28 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and its whole notice is «Δεν έχουμε λεπτομέρειες για τον βίο του Αγίου». So the see and the rank are all the page gives: no year, so no `dates` object, and no place beyond Serbia. He is kept on the same day as two patriarchs of Constantinople of the same name, Arsenios Autoreianos among them, and nothing on the page joins him to either. The corpus holds no archbishop of Serbia of this name. No hymn. No asterisk and not the sentence «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη η ύπαρξη του Αγίου».

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 10.11.2025 (28. октобар ст. ст.) — „Св. Арсеније архиепископ Пећски.“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry and the longest on it, one person, quoted whole with its closing full stop (section 4). «архиепископ» is the `archbishop` this folder holds and the body’s «Велики јерарх» the `hierarch` beside it, so `types` is untouched; «игуман» would map to `abbot`, and it is NOT added, because the abbacy of Žiča is a post he held on the way and not a grade the calendar gives him — the heading ranks him archbishop. `dates` UNTOUCHED AND THE BOOK CONFIRMS THE YEAR AND ADDS THE DAY. The folder holds `death` 1266, basis `attested`, off the Russian calendar’s «(1266)» and its two lives’ «в 1266 г.» This entry says «упокојио се у Господу 28. окт. 1266. год.» — the same year, with the day of the month added, which is the day of the row itself. Nothing to change; the confirmation is recorded because three books now agree on a thirteenth-century Serbian year, which is unusual in this corpus. THE THIRTY YEARS WERE NOT TURNED INTO A DATE. «Мудро управљао црквом 30 година» would put the start of his archiepiscopate at 1236, which is also the year this corpus records for Sava’s death at Trnovo. The subtraction is not in the book and no `floruit` was written from it. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS, AND IT IS THE WHOLE SHAPE OF HIS LIFE. He was BORN IN SREM and was TONSURED WHILE STILL YOUNG, giving himself sincerely to the struggle for the salvation of his soul; hearing of Sava he WENT TO HIM AT ŽIČA, where Sava received him kindly and ENROLLED HIM IN THE BROTHERHOOD, and SOON MADE HIM ABBOT of it for the rare virtues he saw in him. WHEN THE HUNGARIANS ATTACKED THE SERBIAN LANDS SAVA SENT HIM SOUTH to find the archbishopric a place more sheltered than Žiča, AND HE CHOSE PEĆ, where he built a monastery and a church to the holy apostles, LATER CALLED THE CHURCH OF THE LORD’S ASCENSION. Before his second departure for Jerusalem SAVA APPOINTED HIM HIS SUCCESSOR on the archiepiscopal throne. And when Sava died at Trnovo on the way back, ARSENIUS PRESSED KING VLADISLAV TO BRING SAVA’S BODY HOME to the Serbian land. The entry closes with the inscription that stands on the altar wall of the church at Peć, printed in this book’s own Church Slavonic orthography: „Господи Боже нашъ вонми, посяти и благослови храмъ сей… помените же и мене гряшнаго Арсенија“ — and says he is buried there. TWO `related` ROWS, BOTH RECIPROCATED IN THIS COMMIT, AND BOTH EARNED BY AN ACT THE ENTRY NARRATES. `sava-of-serbia` received him, made him abbot, sent him to Peć and named him successor; `vladislav-of-serbia` is the king he pressed over Sava’s body. Neither is a dedication and neither is a shared day. The folder’s existing row to `sava-the-second` is untouched. Srem, Žiča, Peć, Trnovo and Jerusalem are named and none is proposed as a coordinate; no `locations`. The `office` «Archbishop of Serbia» already on the folder is untouched — this book says Пећски, of Peć, which is the see’s seat and not a different see, and an office is not a reader’s to rewrite. THE FORM FOLDS AND THE FOLD IS KEYED: «Арсеније» is already held by `arsenius-of-corfu` and `arsenius-the-great`, so this takes the key from two folders to three. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day’s verse is Bishop Nikolai’s own and is about Arsenius.

death.note: days.pravoslavie.ru prints «(1266)» after his name on 28 октября ст. ст., and both of his life pages give the year in words: «святитель мирно скончался в 1266 г.» and «святой отошел ко Господу в 1266 году». The Greek page this folder was written from gives no year.

hymns.text: Милости наставниче и благоутробия сокровище,/ еже всем отверзл еси,/ правоверия учителю и архиереев Божественное удобрение,/ отче наш, иерарше Арсение,/ нищих был еси заступник:/ тем моли Христа Бога,/ просветити души наша, да не когда уснем в смерть.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 28 октября ст. ст. — «Тропарь святителя Арсения, архиепископа Сербского»

english.text: Teacher of mercy and treasury of compassion, which you opened to all; teacher of right belief and divine adornment of bishops, our father, hierarch Arsenius, you were the defender of the poor. Therefore pray to Christ God to enlighten our souls, that we never fall asleep in death.

hymns.text: В пищи словес твоих, Богоносе Арсение,/ разумно чада твоя питая,/ языком хваля, устнами же пение принося, вещанием зовый:/ Христе, Ты еси Свет неизреченный.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 28 октября ст. ст. — «Кондак святителя Арсения, архиепископа Сербского»

english.text: Feeding your children with understanding on the food of your words, God-bearing Arsenius, praising with your tongue and offering up song with your lips, you called aloud: Christ, you are the Light unutterable.
